references.text: Describes the showbread that was to be placed on the table before the Lord at all times, the same context as Leviticus 24:6.
Moses arranged the bread on the table before the Lord, a direct fulfillment of the instructions regarding the placement of the showbread.
Mentions the gold table where the showbread was placed in Solomon's temple, serving the same ritual function described in Leviticus.
The Levites were responsible for the showbread and were to set them out every Sabbath, continuing the practice from Leviticus 24.
Describes the regular arrangement of the showbread on the pure gold table, a direct parallel to the pure table mentioned in Leviticus 24:6.
David ate the showbread that had been removed from before the Lord, referring to the same arrangement of holy bread.
Mentions the table and the showbread as part of the furnishings of the tabernacle in the Holy Place, confirming the Old Testament arrangement.
